brief: Ahead of the midterms, GS re-circulates desk views. The actionable question is not which Democratic priorities become law but which policy areas become easier to negotiate, draw regulatory attention, or gain leverage in future spending fights. The House passed a CR funding government through December 11, avoiding a shutdown. Affordability is a theme on both sides. Expired enhanced ACA subsidies have raised premiums and cut marketplace enrollment, pressuring insurers and raising hospital uncompensated care, so GS is long ACA-exposed beneficiaries. It is short drug-makers on bipartisan Medicare-negotiation and MFN-pricing pressure, flagging MRK and AMGN exposure. On AI power costs, GS calls the ratepayer-protection debate underappreciated. It is long renewables, grid infrastructure and Power Up America, hedged with protection on hyperscalers and datacenter equipment. GS is long non-defense government spending and short defense spending into the December CR deadline. Corporate tax, with its 21% rate and 100% bonus depreciation made permanent, is insulated through 2028 under either outcome, with valuation risk beyond 2029 if rates rose. Additional risks flagged: antitrust (short Big Tech), financial regulation (short investment banks and crypto equities), tariffs seen rising rather than falling into 2027 (short tariff-sensitive names), and housing (long homebuilders).
